nature: exploratory and descriptive; run at B's explicit request after the pre-check verdict 'stop'. It answers 'how much of the hard-label switching is measurement noise', not coverage. No decision depends on it. Idea borrowed from Netzer, Lattin & Srinivasan (2008) at abstract level only.

data.sequence: monthly counts of distinct valid orders (is_valid_rfm_order == 1, identified customer) for the 12 calendar months 2009-12 .. 2010-11 (orders before 2010-12-01 only)
data.selection_note: every customer has >= 1 valid order in months 1-6 by construction (Profile customers); this conditions the first half of each sequence and is reported, not corrected

models.M1: K-state Poisson HMM, homogeneous transition matrix, parameters shared by all customers (no hierarchical Bayes); initial distribution estimated
models.M2_season_emission: M1 + one multiplicative peak effect on every state's Poisson mean in the peak months Sep, Oct, Nov 2010
models.M3_season_transition: M1 with a separate transition matrix for transitions INTO the peak months
models.K: 3 for all models (primary, matches K-means); M1 also fitted with K = 2 and 4 (descriptive)
models.state_order: states renumbered by ascending off-peak Poisson mean (state 0 = least active)

fitting.algorithm: EM (Baum-Welch with scaled forward-backward), numpy/scipy implementation in src/online_trade/future_a/hmm.py (hmmlearn is not installed)
fitting.starts: 20 random starts, seeds 0-19; keep the highest log-likelihood
fitting.model_comparison: BIC = -2 logL + p ln(n_obs), n_obs = 2,684 x 12; descriptive

simulation_check.how: simulate 2,684 sequences of length 12 from the fitted K=3 M1 parameters (seed 12345), refit with the same procedure
simulation_check.pass: after matching states by mean, max absolute error of transition probabilities < 0.05 and max relative error of Poisson means < 10%; a failure is reported and the HMM results are labelled unreliable

outputs_descriptive: parameters, log-likelihood, BIC of every model
monthly transition matrix, persistence per state, stationary-share-weighted diagonal (compared descriptively with Chen et al. 2019's 0.85)
filtered state posteriors (forward only, no look-ahead) at month 6 (May 2010, end of Profile) and month 12 (Nov 2010, end of Discovery); MAP-state switch share between them; Viterbi switch share

noise indicator: 1 - (HMM filtered-MAP switch share / hard-label switch share 48.7% from pre-check P1), with the caveat that HMM states (monthly activity) and K-means clusters (RFM) are different partitions
correspondence: frozen K-means labels x filtered MAP state at month 6; pre-check P1 labels x filtered MAP state at month 12; counts, Hungarian-aligned agreement and kappa
share of customers whose maximum filtered posterior at month 12 is >= 0.8
known_information_before_registration: Pre-check P1-P4 results (hard-label 6-month retention 51.3%, i.e. switch 48.7%; drift curve; silence 28% in Discovery).
No HMM had been fitted on these data.
